subject: Discovery: Client workload profile and SLO gaps (tokens/QPS/streaming)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Moreno <alicia@cloudretail.ai>, Dan Warner <dan.warner@zephyrs.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery follow-up: workload profile and SLO details we discussed

Hi Alicia / Dan —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap focused on the performance / SLO items we need to size a Dedicated or Private deployment and to propose a realistic canary run later this month. I attached a small workload template (cloudretail_workload_template.xlsx) — filling it out will let us produce a token/sec & QPS sizing estimate.

What we need to confirm (short bullets preferred):
- Target latency SLOs (p50 / p95) for user-facing generation and for streaming-first-token. If you have both interactive UI and async batch endpoints, please flag which is which.
- Typical tokens per request: median and 95th percentile (tokens in prompt + model output).
- Expected average QPS (steady-state) and typical peak QPS (and duration of peak windows — minutes/hours).
- Concurrent active sessions (how many user sessions will hold an open chat window / KV cache).
- Streaming requirement: do you need partial tokens every ~50–200ms, or is 500–1000ms acceptable? Also whether clients open long-lived websockets.
- Any long tail workloads (e.g., large document summarization) that spike tokens/request > 5k — if so, frequency per day.

Initial thought from our side (very rough until we get numbers): if steady-state QPS is low (single digits) but you have regular 3–8 minute bursts at 40–60 QPS and 1–2k tokens/request, we’ll recommend reserved pool with burst capacity and prefix caching. If you have sustained 50+ QPS for many hours, a Dedicated cluster sizing will be needed.

Next steps: please populate the template and reply with the numbers by EOD Friday PT. We can then propose a canary test plan (2-day window) and a preliminary capacity/price estimate.

Thanks —
Jonas
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: workload profile and SLO details we discussed

Jonas — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a small telemetry extract and I filled the template with our best estimates (see cloudretail_telemetry_sample.csv + template). Summary here so it’s easy to scan:

- Latency SLOs:
  - Interactive search (UI product): p50 target ~120ms, p95 target ~650ms (end-to-end generation).
  - Streaming / typing experience: first partial token within 220ms, subsequent tokens streamed ~80ms/token is ideal; if not achievable p95 <= 500ms is acceptable.
- Tokens per request:
  - Median total tokens (prompt + response): ~620 tokens
  - 95th percentile tokens/request: ~2,100 tokens (happens ~3% of calls, particularly during summarization workflows)
  - Long tail >5k tokens: very rare — ~10 calls/day during nightly ingestion jobs (non-interactive).
- QPS and peak profile:
  - Steady-state QPS: 4–6 QPS (normal business hours)
  - Peak QPS (promotion spikes / checkout assistance): up to 52 QPS sustained for ~8–12 minutes, multiple times per day during promotions; we've seen a single-event spike up to ~120 QPS for ~90 seconds.
- Concurrency:
  - Active concurrent chat sessions holding state: ~1,100 during peak retail hours; typical session TTL ~45 minutes.
- Streaming/connectivity:
  - Clients use websockets for the UI; need partial token streaming and session affinity so KV cache is reused across messages.

Other notes: authentication is handled via our gateway; we can support mTLS for private deployments. We do have SOC2 reports and can share them through your secure portal if helpful.

Let us know if you want the raw telemetry in a different format. We’re flexible on the canary date but prefer something during a low-traffic window (weekend early morning PT).

Best,
Alicia Moreno
Head of AI Platform, CloudRetail
alicia@cloudretail.ai

Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: workload profile and SLO details we discussed

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the telemetry, Alicia — this is exactly what we need. Quick readouts and planned next steps: 

1) Sizing implication (rough): with median 620 tokens and peak bursts up to 52 QPS for ~10 minutes, plus that rare 120-QPS blip, we’ll likely recommend a Dedicated pool sized for steady-state + predictable burst (autoscaling with short warm pools) — or a Hosted + Dedicated hybrid where bursts route to reserved burst capacity. We’ll model both options.

2) Streaming/latency: the smoking gun is your first-token target (220ms) + 80ms/token streaming — we can hit those with our streaming-optimized kernels if we pin a lower-latency model variant and tune batching. We’ll call this out as a must-have in the canary.

3) Session affinity / KV cache: Grace, Priyom — can you confirm we have an answer for sticky routing vs. global KV sharing? For the canary I suggest we start with per-session affinity to maximize KV hit rates.

4) Canary proposal: 48-hour window on a weekend (we suggest Sat–Sun, 02:00–06:00 PT local low-traffic window) where we ramp through: 1 QPS -> steady 6 QPS -> 52 QPS sustained for 10 min -> 120 QPS 90s blast. We'll coordinate synthetic traffic and a small subset of real traffic if CloudRetail is comfortable.

5) Data & compliance: Alicia — thanks for SOC2 note. For Private deployment we'll need an initial security questionnaire and your preferred KMS option (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed).

If that plan looks fine I’ll draft the canary runbook + success criteria and share a calendar invite for the planning call next week.

Best,
Jonas

Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: workload profile and SLO details we discussed

Quick technical follow-up from my side so we capture it in the runbook: 

- Session affinity model: agree with per-session affinity for the canary. We'll instrument per-session KV hit-rate and fall back to global cold-start behavior if affinity misses exceed 5% during the test.
- Batching policy: for interactive flows we will cap batching to a 15ms collect window for first token generation to meet the ~220ms first-token target, then allow 80–120ms batching for subsequent token windows.
- Backpressure & queueing: propose a soft-fail threshold at 150 QPS where we return a rate-limited 429 with a Retry-After and route to a cheaper model variant as fallback.

I'll add these to the runbook draft. Jonas — if you want I can take the first pass on the canary playbook and share by Monday.

—Grace
